title: Neuroblastoma: treatment by INRG risk group
alt: After staging and biology define the risk group, low-risk disease is usually treated with surgery alone and observation, intermediate risk with surgery plus 4 to 8 chemotherapy cycles, and high risk with intensive induction, surgery, high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue, radiotherapy and dinutuximab-based maintenance, so survival falls from over 95% to about 50%.
caption: Framework follows INRG/COG risk stratification; exact regimens follow the local protocol.

nodes.text: Assign INRG risk group from stage, age, MYCN, histology and ploidy
Low risk: complete resection, or observation alone for asymptomatic 4S and small adrenal masses; chemotherapy only if symptomatic or progressing
Intermediate risk: resection before or after 4 to 8 cycles of moderate-intensity chemotherapy; radiotherapy only for residual or symptomatic disease
High risk: intensive induction chemotherapy (cisplatin/etoposide, cyclophosphamide/doxorubicin), then resection of the primary
Consolidation: high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell rescue (tandem courses), then radiotherapy to tumour bed and residual metastases
Maintenance: isotretinoin for 6 cycles plus dinutuximab anti-GD2 immunotherapy
5-year event-free survival about 50%; relapse is common
